subject: Renewal: Stratus Labs — ramped credits & short-term price hold
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit@stratuslabs.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@stratuslabs.io
Date: 2026-06-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal conversation — need short-term flexibility

Jordan,

Thanks for the call this morning. Stratus is happy with performance but the finance team is nervous about the step-up in committed spend for year 3. Two asks from my side: 1) a short-term (6 month) price hold at current blended rates to cover the renewal execution window, and 2) a structured credit that converts to committed capacity if we choose the 24-month option.

High level: we want to commit to an uplift in Q3 (+30% tokens) but need a staged glide path and an explicit fall-back (temporary credit) if consumption lags. Can you share a sketch of how Redwood would model the credit conversion and any limitations around burst capacity?

I can loop in procurement formally once we have an outline.

Thanks,
Amit
Amit Shah
Head of ML Platforms, Stratus Labs

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Shah <amit@stratuslabs.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — need short-term flexibility

Amit — thanks for the clarity and for being candid about finance timelines. High-level proposal attached (see: 2026-06-14-pricing-workback.xlsx). Quick summary here so we have a working draft for procurement: 

- 6-month price hold: keep current blended effective rate for six months following renewal signature.
- Staged uplift: commit to +30% baseline capacity with a 3-month ramp (10% / month).
- Conversion credit: upfront credit equal to 10% of the first-year committed value. If customer signs a 24-month extension within 90 days, that credit converts and amortizes against committed spend; otherwise it reverts to non-refundable usage credit for the first 6 months.
- Burst capacity: we can guarantee burst up to 2.5x baseline for short windows; burst above that is billed at on-demand rates.

Marissa and Kim — can you confirm the legal/commercial constraints on the conversion language and whether Finance needs a different amortization schedule?

If this works directionally, Amit, we can produce a short LOI and procurement checklist.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Amit Shah <amit@stratuslabs.io>
Date: 2026-06-14T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — need short-term flexibility

On Mon, Jun 11, 2026 at 11:03 AM Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Amit — thanks for the clarity and for being candid about finance timelines. High-level proposal attached (see: 2026-06-14-pricing-workback.xlsx). Quick summary here so we have a working draft for procurement: 
> 
> - 6-month price hold: keep current blended effective rate for six months following renewal signature.
> - Staged uplift: commit to +30% baseline capacity with a 3-month ramp (10% / month).
> - Conversion credit: upfront credit equal to 10% of the first-year committed value. If customer signs a 24-month extension within 90 days, that credit converts and amortizes against committed spend; otherwise it reverts to non-refundable usage credit for the first 6 months.
> - Burst capacity: we can guarantee burst up to 2.5x baseline for short windows; burst above that is billed at on-demand rates.

Jordan / team — commercial ok but legal needs the conversion language tightened. Two recommended edits: 
1) Make the credit conversion conditional on both signature of the 24-month term AND the customer meeting a minimum 12-month ARR threshold (simple clause to avoid conversion abuse).
2) Define the amortization as quarterly credits applied against invoice (not retroactive).

I also added a fallback clause: if usage for the first 6 months is <85% of the ramped baseline, Redwood will allow a one-time true-up reduction (up to 15%) to the following quarter's committed baseline — this protects Stratus while keeping incentive intact.

Attaching an updated workbook with the amortization schedule and example invoices.

Attachments: 2026-06-14-pricing-workback.xlsx (xlsx)

Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: Amit Shah <amit@stratuslabs.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@stratuslabs.io
Date: 2026-06-15T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — need short-term flexibility

Thanks, Jordan and Marissa — this is much closer to what we need. Procurement wants the LOI and the explicit conversion mechanics so they can route to legal. Two quick asks before we route: 

- Can the conversion credit be split 60/40: 60% applied to committed spend in the first year, 40% to Year 2, if we sign 24 months? That helps our cash planning.
- Can Redwood confirm SLA credit treatment during the 6-month price hold (i.e., do the same SLA terms and uptime credits apply)?

If you can confirm those two items we will route the LOI this week and aim for a July 1 signature. Happy to hop on a 20-min call if needed.

Procurement copied for visibility: procurement@stratuslabs.io

Regards,
Amit
